class_id: a cross-check that scopes one side of a comparison but not the other reports every out-of-scope member as missing
feature: any two-directional cross-check between OUR data and an external oracle feed, where one direction filters its own side to a narrower population (a segment, a source, a status) but the other direction walks the oracle's FULL feed unfiltered
symptom: direction A (what we publish, checked against the oracle) is deliberately scoped to a subset of our rows -- reasonable, since only that subset is expected to appear on the oracle's feed. Direction B (what the oracle publishes, checked against us) reuses THAT SAME scoped lookup set to decide whether we already have a row for an oracle entry, instead of building its lookup from every row we publish. Any oracle entry belonging to the population direction A excluded is then structurally invisible to direction B's lookup and is reported as 'we have no row for it at all', even though the row exists -- because the check never looked outside the narrower set to find it. The false premise compounds the bug: the narrowing is often justified by a claim that the excluded population 'never appears' on the oracle feed, a claim nobody re-verified after the oracle's feed changed or was never true to begin with.
first_seen: 2026-09-23 -- IPODhan `crossCheckNseStatuses` (scripts/lib/detection-floor-checks.mjs), issue #895. Direction 2 built `openByKey`/`knownByKey` from `scoped = ourRows.filter(inScope)`, where `inScope` keeps MAINBOARD rows only, then walked EVERY row of NSE's live current-issue and upcoming feeds. The scope comment claimed 'NSE SME (Emerge) issues ... legitimately never appear on these endpoints' -- false: the prod floor run of 2026-09-23 03:46 IST saw 3 SME issues on NSE's feeds (Himalayan Solar Limited, Pooja Logistics Limited, Coreintegra Consulting Services Limited), all three existing in our data with the correct status, all three reported as 'we have no row for it at all' every night this ran.
fix_prs: the class-level fix is to build the oracle-matching direction's lookup set from EVERY row on our side that could plausibly appear on the oracle feed, never from the other direction's narrower scoped set -- the two directions have different, independently-justified populations, and one must not silently inherit the other's filter. Direction 1 (ours-checked-against-oracle) may legitimately stay narrow when its own noise argument holds; direction 2 (oracle-checked-against-ours) must not reuse that narrowing as its own lookup population. IPODhan fix: scripts/lib/detection-floor-checks.mjs `crossCheckNseStatuses` direction 2 now builds `openByKey`/`knownByKey` from `ourRows` (all OPEN/UPCOMING rows the caller passes in), not `scoped`. Direction 1 stays MAINBOARD-scoped by choice, pinned by a regression test
detection_check: scripts/tests/audit-detection-floor.test.mjs '(l) #895 ...' tests (4 cases: SME UPCOMING row matches NSE upcoming feed with zero mismatches; SME OPEN row matches NSE current-issue feed with zero mismatches; a genuinely missing company is still discriminated as a FAIL; direction 1 stays MAINBOARD-scoped and does not also fire its own message for the same row) exercise the REAL exported `crossCheckNseStatuses`, red before the fix, green after, mutation-proof (reverting the one-line fix flips them red again). Generalisable check for any two-directional cross-check: assert that the oracle-matching direction's lookup population is built from the SAME unfiltered set the write path actually publishes, not from the other direction's scoped subset
